posts.headline: North American Scrabble Championship comes to Cedar Rapids

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: link preview does the work and the hook is one line

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: the ballroom scene needs a sentence of setup, and the Cedar Rapids angle is local

posts.blurb: Three hundred competitive Scrabble players took over a Cedar Rapids hotel ballroom, hunting nine- to eleven-letter words. One opened with echeveria. Sit down at the board and everyone is equal.
posts.why: A national championship played on folding tables by people who drove in from everywhere — competition with no spectators and total seriousness.

posts.headline: European Sleeper launches new international night train from Paris to Brussels and Hamburg

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: route, fare and date in one line — the link is the payload

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: the Scandinavia connection needs a sentence before the fare earns the click

posts.blurb: Since July 13 you can board in Paris at night and get off in Hamburg, via Brussels and Liege, from 69.99 euros in a shared compartment. Copenhagen and Oslo are one connection further on.
posts.why: Arriving somewhere on foot with the whole day ahead of you is exactly the shape of a route — and night trains keep coming back.

posts.headline: Grand reopening set for revived Landmark Saloon after regulars save beloved Portland bar

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: hometown bar story, and the audience there skews local and older

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: closed in February, reopened in July — the turn fits one line

posts.blurb: Portland's Landmark Saloon closed in February. Two longtime regulars bought it with the old owner's help, kept the live local bands, renamed it Switchback and reopened on SE Division in July.
posts.why: A neighbourhood live-music room saved by the people who drank in it — the kind of place worth routing a stop past.

posts.headline: Roman villa with intricate mosaic and bath house

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: twelve square metres of red, white and blue tesserae carries it with no caption — feed post

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: detectorist finds tiles, archaeologists find a villa — link preview does the rest

platforms.name: Facebook
platforms.why: the 2004-to-now gap needs a sentence, and the museum ending gives it a landing

posts.blurb: A metal detectorist flagged something in a Devon field in 2004. Archaeologists have now lifted a fourth-century mosaic out of it, the furthest west one has ever been found in a Roman British villa.
posts.why: Someone noticed a detail on the ground and it took twenty-two years to pay off — the patient version of what our players do in an afternoon.

posts.headline: Watch: Man balances 195 rolls of toilet paper on his head for 30 seconds

platforms.name: X
platforms.why: one absurd number and a clip, link preview does the work

platforms.name: Instagram
platforms.why: a man under a tower of 195 rolls stands on the image alone — feed post

posts.blurb: David Rush of Idaho set the toilet-paper-balancing record at 101, lost it to someone who stacked 152, and has taken it back with 195 rolls on his forehead. He says the enemy in this sport is nerves.
posts.why: A record nobody asked for, contested seriously by strangers over five years — people competing at something strange is our whole beat.
